body:
## Summary

This PR records

$$\mu^{\mathrm S}_3 \ \ge\ (64728+\sqrt{3018723123})^{1/26} \ =\ 1.5678599024\ldots,$$

which improves the listed value $(1042+2\sqrt{261207})^{1/17} = 1.5666969787\ldots$ [Cla2026] and the value $(1127+\sqrt{925536})^{1/17} = 1.5678015201\ldots$ proposed in the open PR #237 [Syl2026]. It appends one row to the lower-bound table of `constants/49a.md`, adds the [Kos2026] reference and a contribution note, and updates the README cell for constant 49 and "Recent progress". Markdown only. Like the [IRSI2026], [Cla2026] and [Syl2026] rows, the bound is the limit of an infinite gluing chain counted by a $2\times 2$ transfer matrix, not a single finite family, so it carries the asterisk.

## Construction

Take the two base families of [Cla2026]:
- $F$: 75 sets on the 10 edges of $K_5$ (the 5 stars, the 10 graphs $K_{2,3}$, and the 60 graphs whose complement is a chair);
- $H$: 121 sets on $\mathbb{Z}_{11}$ (the images of $\{0,\dots,6\}$, $\{0,1,2,3,4,6,7\}$, $\{0,1,2,6,9\}$ under $x\mapsto ax+b$, $a$ a nonzero square).

**Two pendants.** Glue a copy $H_1$ of $H$ (at $0$) to $F$ at the edge $(0,3)$, and a second copy $H_2$ at the edge $(0,4)$, by the gluing lemma ([DEGKM1997], Lemma 4.4). For $C\in F$ the $H_i$-part of a product set is $D$ with $D\in H$, $0\notin D$ (46 choices) if the glue edge lies in $C$, and $D\setminus\{0\}$ with $0\in D\in H$ (75 choices) otherwise. This gives 250659 sets on $8+10+10 = 28$ points.

**Augmentation at both pendants.** As in #237, we add sets whose part in a pendant is empty. At $H_1$ we add the 15 edge sets $T\subseteq E(K_5)\setminus\{(0,3)\}$ listed in the artefact, each combined with every $H_2$-part allowed by whether $(0,4)\in T$ (806 sets). Symmetrically we add 15 sets at $H_2$ (806 sets).

**Augmentation inside $H_1$.** Finally we add 20 sets that lie inside $H_1$, with no $K_5$ part and no $H_2$ part (listed in the artefact). They are $H$'s own augmentation sets at its root $0$, with the rest of the block in the role of the pendant. We chose them from the 171 subsets of $H_1$'s points that pass the single-set test; an integer program over $H$'s conflicts finds no larger compatible choice. They contain neither port. Only one pendant can take them: a set inside $H_1$, a set inside $H_2$ and an $H_2$-side addition can be pairwise disjoint, which is a sunflower with empty kernel.

**One more set.** Finally we add the set $\{(1,2),(1,4),(2,3)\}\cup H_2$: three $K_5$ edges and all ten points of $H_2$, with an empty $H_1$-part. It contains neither port. An enumeration of every set inside $K_5$-part $\cup H_1$ and inside $K_5$-part $\cup H_2$ found it as the only set that can still be added on its own. Total: 252292 sets. The family is maximal under single additions in those regions.

Why this works (this explains the construction and is not used in the proof):
- Any two members of $H$ have intersecting parts away from $0$. So a set with an empty $H_1$-part can neither contain a product set nor form a sunflower with two of them; only conditions on the $K_5$ side remain, exactly as in #237.
- Additions at different pendants never conflict. Take $X$ with an empty $H_1$-part and $X'$ with an empty $H_2$-part. Two additions at $H_1$ intersect inside $H_2$, while each of them meets $X'$ outside $H_2$. So no triple mixing the two kinds is a sunflower, and neither kind contains the other.
- The 15 sets at each pendant were re-optimized for the two-pendant port weights.
- The 20 sets inside $H_1$ and the one extra set are checked directly: `verify.py` checks every pair and triple through them exhaustively, in pure Python.

**Chain.** Chain copies of the 252292-set family with in-port $(0,1)$ and out-port $(0,2)$:

| | $N_{00}$ | $N_{01}=N_{10}$ | $N_{11}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| product sets | 33948 | 64360 | 87991 |
| additions at $H_1$ | 0 | 184 | 438 |
| additions at $H_2$ | 0 | 184 | 438 |
| sets inside $H_1$ | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| the extra set | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| total | 33969 | 64728 | 88867 |

$T$ has rows $(64728, 88867)$ and $(33969, 64728)$, with Perron root $\rho = 64728+\sqrt{88867\cdot 33969} = 64728+\sqrt{3018723123}\approx 119670.9078$. The $k$-th chain family is Sperner and sunflower-free on $26k+2$ points and has at least $c\rho^k$ members. Since the limit defining $\mu^{\mathrm S}_3$ exists, $\mu^{\mathrm S}_3\ge\rho^{1/26}$.

## Exact comparisons (integer arithmetic)

We have $\lfloor\sqrt{3018723123}\rfloor = 54942$, so $\rho > 119670$.
- **Against #237** (17 points per period). $\rho'=1127+\sqrt{925536} < 1127+963 = 2090$. The claim $\rho^{1/26} > \rho'^{1/17}$ is equivalent to $\rho^{17} > \rho'^{26}$, which follows from $119670^{17} > 2090^{26}$, an inequality between two 87-digit integers.
- **Against [Cla2026]** (17 points per period). $\rho''=1042+\sqrt{1044828} < 1042+1023 = 2065$, and $119670^{17} > 2065^{26}$.
- **Interval.** With $L=\lfloor 10^6\cdot 64728+\sqrt{3018723123\cdot 10^{12}}\rfloor = 119670907849$, we have $L/10^6 < \rho < (L+1)/10^6$. Then $15678599024^{26}\cdot 10^{6} < L\cdot 10^{260}$ and $15678599025^{26}\cdot 10^{6} > (L+1)\cdot 10^{260}$, so $1.5678599024 < \rho^{1/26} < 1.5678599025$.

## Verification

The bound needs only one fact: the 252292-set block is Sperner and 3-sunflower-free. (Sperner is a hypothesis of the gluing lemma, not part of the definition of $\mu^{\mathrm S}_3$.) The rest is the chain argument already used in the [IRSI2026], [Cla2026] and [Syl2026] rows.
- **Exhaustive check, C.** `check.c` (about 150 lines of C, optional OpenMP, no other dependencies) groups the other members by their intersection with $S$, for each member $S$. This covers every triple. It takes about 15 minutes on 2 threads and prints `OK 252292`. It rejects planted duplicates, containments, sunflowers and malformed input, and agrees with brute force on 248 near-valid random families.
- **Independent check.** A second Claude agent wrote its own checker (`verify_independent.py`, numba) from the certificate format specification only, with no access to the construction code. It verified all 252292 sets exhaustively in 10m54s and recomputed the port counts and $\rho$ exactly, with rate $1.5678599024245898858529\ldots$. It also verified the two earlier versions of the block exhaustively: 252271 sets at rate $1.5678513426905297499\ldots$, where it also rejected a full-size planted-sunflower control, and 252291 sets at rate $1.5678594949047002997\ldots$, in 11m38s.
- **Rebuild, standard-library Python.** `verify.py` does the following:
  - rebuilds $F$ and $H$ from their definitions and the block from the description above, and checks that it equals the certificate's block as a set (`SHA256SUMS` pins the file itself);
  - checks $F$ and $H$ exhaustively, and checks the pairwise-intersection property of $H$;
  - checks the core-level conditions of the augmentation lemma for the 15+15 added sets;
  - checks every pair and triple through the 20 sets inside $H_1$ and through the extra set exhaustively;
  - recomputes the port counts and proves the comparisons above with integers.

  A full triple check of 252k sets is not practical in pure Python (about $3\cdot 10^{10}$ bucket operations), so that part is left to `check.c` and `verify_independent.py`.

## How to reproduce

```
git clone https://github.com/DennisKoshta/sunflower3-49a-certificate && cd sunflower3-49a-certificate && git checkout c4ee81737f9f
xz -dk two_pendant_extra_1.5678599.txt.xz          # keeps the .xz; writes the .txt
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS                            # all OK; the .txt line is 10ee18f9...4838
python3 verify.py two_pendant_extra_1.5678599.txt.xz --pure --extra   # stdlib; rebuild + lemma hypotheses + exhaustive check through the 21 added sets + exact comparisons, ~20 s; ALL CHECKS PASS
cc -O2 -fopenmp check.c -o check
xz -dc two_pendant_extra_1.5678599.txt.xz | ./check    # exhaustive; OK 252292, ALL BLOCKS OK (about 15 min on 2 threads)
python3 verify_independent.py two_pendant_extra_1.5678599.txt   # second exhaustive checker (numpy/numba/mpmath), uncompressed file, about 11 min
```

## Credits

- Deuber, Erdős, Gunderson, Kostochka and Meyer [DEGKM1997], for the gluing lemma.
- [IRSI2026] (https://github.com/Aspect5/sunflower-free-capacity), for the exact $2\times 2$ transfer-matrix count of the chain.
- [Cla2026] (https://github.com/joshua17-create/sunflower-lower-bound), for the families $F$ and $H$.
- Sylla [Syl2026] / PR #237 (https://github.com/xSyllaa/sunflower-pendant-chain), for gluing $H$ to $F$ as a pendant and for the idea of augmenting with sets whose pendant part is empty. This PR applies that idea at two pendants at once, and inside a pendant.
- T. Tao and contributors, for this table.

## Disclosure (AI use)

Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) found the construction by computer search and wrote the certificate, the checkers and this text, directed by Dennis Koshta, who takes responsibility for the submission. The independent check was done by a separate Claude agent working from the format specification only. The result is not peer-reviewed, and no human mathematician has checked the argument.
